definition: Alacrity means cheerful eagerness and promptness.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word alacrity. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know alacrity should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Asked who would lead the campus tour for the visiting families, Jae sprang up with alacrity, already reaching for the map bin.
Willingness only means you won't refuse; you can be willing and still sigh, stall, and go last, while alacrity means you move first and gladly.
Promptness gets you there on time with a neutral face; alacrity goes further, adding unmistakable delight to the speed.

Eagerness is the wanting itself - a strong desire to do or get something that can burn quietly while you never move from your chair. Alacrity is eagerness made visible in action: you are up at once, and the speed itself shows the delight.

Readiness means you are prepared to act - bags packed, plan in hand - whether or not you feel any joy about the job. Alacrity adds the missing feeling: not just standing ready, but springing forward cheerfully the instant the request comes.

Enthusiasm is excited, energetic interest, and it can spend itself entirely in talk about the thing. Alacrity is narrower: the excitement has to show up as immediate, cheerful movement. An enthusiastic fan chats about the club all day; a fan with alacrity is first in line to volunteer.
a dragging of the feet, wishing not to act
slowness of movement or response
The conductor flipped the score to the final movement, marked allegro, and raised her baton.
Alacrity means cheerful eagerness and promptness.
When the food pantry's freezer failed at closing time, the manager asked whether anyone could drive the donations across town that night.
Before she finished the sentence, Camila had answered with alacrity: van keys in hand, door propped open, humming as she loaded the first crate.
Alacrity is more precise than eagerness or promptness alone because it names both at once - the quickness of the response and the visible cheerfulness behind it.
Camila isn't just fast, and she isn't just willing; she is plainly delighted to be fast.
Alacrity is a polished word for the everyday pairing of speed and cheer.
In casual talk, 'eagerly' or 'right away' does the job; reach for alacrity when you want a single word to show that someone's quickness itself revealed their delight.

Every small town has one: the volunteer who reaches the firehouse before the siren finishes its first climb, and arrives glad to have been called.
In Maple Falls that is Ruth Ferreira, a retired mail carrier who has answered pages for thirty-one years.
What the younger volunteers notice is not her speed alone but her mood.
She arrives grinning, boots already laced, teasing the crew as she swings into the truck.
Chiefs call that quality alacrity, and they prize it, because a crew takes its temperature from the first face through the door.
Ruth's own explanation is simpler.
Some people are asked to help, she says, and feel lucky about it.
